message.content: Process image-resize jobs in the background, retrying any job that fails. Create what is needed and name it demo-image-jobs.

content.text: Queue ID isn't known in dry-run, so I use a placeholder.

I set up the queue `demo-image-jobs`, a second queue `demo-image-jobs-dlq` for jobs that keep failing, and a Worker `demo-image-jobs`. The Worker accepts `{ key, width }` jobs over POST and puts them on the queue. Its queue handler resizes each image from `demo-bucket` using the Images binding, writes the result to `resized/<width>/<key>`, and retries failed jobs with exponential backoff. I also added that Worker as the queue's consumer: batches of 10, up to 5 retries, then the job goes to `demo-image-jobs-dlq`.

Every call was a dry run, so nothing was actually created. The consumer call uses a placeholder queue ID, `demo-image-jobs-queue-id`, because the create-queue call didn't return a real one.
